item.text: I’ll add only remembered candidates that are distinct from the existing proposals, then save the follow-up file without reading or checking it.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec4/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.12	faith and patience inheriting the promise	The commentary's exception begins with belief and ends with mutual counsel to sabr; Hebrews urges imitation of those who inherit the promises through faith and patience. This gives the faith-patience pairing a concrete inheritance horizon.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.7	perseverance in doing good	The commentary pairs righteous deeds with patience; Paul describes those who seek glory and immortality through endurance in good work and receive eternal life. It joins ethical action and perseverance in a judgment setting.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.24	mutually spurring love and good works	The commentary says believers repeatedly counsel one another and do righteous deeds; Hebrews asks the community to consider how to stir one another to love and good works. This is a distinct reciprocal-action detail from the encouragement in Hebrews 10:25.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.38.9	Jeremiah lowered into a cistern to die	The commentary's B002 image is a person held for death; Ebed-Melech says Jeremiah was put in the cistern to die of hunger because no bread remained. The verse supplies an explicit instance of detention with death as its intended outcome.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.7.60	asking that a sin not be held against killers	The commentary says each soul is held to what it has earned; while being stoned, Stephen asks the Lord not to hold this sin against his killers. The dying victim's plea reverses the image of deeds holding a person liable.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.3.9	delayed judgment as patience for repentance	The commentary has the prophet wait for the Lord's judgment; Peter says the Lord's apparent delay is patience, allowing people time to reach repentance rather than perish. It makes waiting itself a merciful postponement of loss.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.12.37	the returning master finds servants watching	The commentary says the one who waits is under observation; Jesus blesses servants whom their returning master finds awake and watching. This gives the watched wait an eschatological household scene and a reward for readiness.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.2.3	waiting for the appointed vision	The commentary defines sabr as waiting for the Lord's decree; Habakkuk says the vision has an appointed time and, even if it seems delayed, the hearer must wait for it. It makes delay part of the promise rather than evidence that it failed.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.40.2	patient waiting and rescue from a pit	The commentary holds self-restraint and being held in tension; the psalmist waits for the LORD, who draws him from a destructive pit and mud. The verse joins patient waiting with release from a concrete form of confinement.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lam.3.26	quiet waiting amid affliction	The commentary opposes sabr to panic and describes waiting for the Lord's judgment; Lamentations says it is good to wait quietly for the LORD's salvation in the aftermath of Jerusalem's ruin. It gives restrained waiting a voice within communal catastrophe.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.34.6	God slow to anger after rebellion	The commentary makes patience restraint and waiting for judgment; after Israel's breach, God describes himself as slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love. It adds divine patience as the quality that makes judgment and renewed relationship coexist.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.30.18	both the Lord and the people wait	The commentary says the prophet must wait for the Lord's decree and that the waiting person remains in God's sight; Isaiah says the LORD waits to show grace and blesses those who wait for him. The reciprocal waiting makes patience an encounter, not a one-sided delay.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	b. Shabbat 88b	enduring insult without answering	The commentary glosses sabr as holding oneself back from panic or outcry; the Talmud praises people who suffer insult without insulting back or replying. Its reading of the lovers of God in Judges 5:31 turns restraint under humiliation into a sign of devotion.
strong	tevrat	motif	Berakhot 60b	reinterpreting apparent loss as hidden good	The commentary presents humanity as being in loss and patience as waiting for God's decree; Rabbi Akiva interprets a chain of setbacks as for the good after those very losses protect his life. This Jewish story preserves trust without pretending the setbacks initially look beneficial.
strong	tevrat	motif	4 Maccabees 6	refusing coerced food at the cost of death	The commentary distinguishes self-restraint from being restrained by another and calls fasting a kind of sabr; Eleazar is pressured to eat forbidden meat but accepts torture rather than violate the law. The martyr narrative makes bodily abstention an act of chosen fidelity under lethal coercion.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.30.18	waiting for grace rather than immediate judgment	The commentary's waiting sabr is directed toward God's ruling; Isaiah links the Lord's waiting to grace and calls those who wait for him blessed. This presents delay as an opening for mercy, distinct from the appointed-vision emphasis in Habakkuk 2:3.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.13.8	delaying the felling for another year	The commentary frames sabr as waiting for the Lord's judgment; in Jesus' fig-tree parable the gardener asks that the unfruitful tree be left for one more year to be dug around and fertilized. The delay gives it time to bear fruit before judgment.
EOF"
